meta.note: Public testdata images only. Per-stage numbers are p50 from full_stage_timing, which runs the complete detector (ChArUco for small/large, plain chessboard for mid, PuzzleBoard for author_like_oblique) on each image.

images.label: Small ChArUco
images.note: A ~0.4 MP ChArUco board (22×22, DICT_4X4_250). The full detector runs corner detection, a chessboard grid build, then per-cell marker decode + board alignment. On a marker-dense board of this size the three stages are close to balanced.

images.label: Mid chessboard
images.note: A plain 11×7 inner-corner chessboard (no markers, so no decode stage). Corner detection is the bulk of the work; the owned grid build is a thin slice.

images.label: Large ChArUco
images.note: A 3 MP ChArUco board (22×22, DICT_4X4_1000). At this resolution corner detection is the largest single stage and the owned grid build is close behind it; the per-cell marker decode, once the dominant cost here, is now the smallest of the three. The published preview is downscaled to 1024 px wide; the detector runs on the full-resolution image.

images.label: PuzzleBoard (synthetic photo)
images.note: A public photo-realistic synthetic PuzzleBoard (20×20): a deterministic render from the canonical 501×501 master maps, warped with perspective, radial distortion, blur, noise and JPEG compression. Unlike the author example photos it decodes uniquely against the current master, so this card runs the full pipeline — corner detection, chessboard grid build, and a real edge-dot decode that recovers every corner's absolute ID on the 501×501 master. The decode stage no longer dominates: the cyclic structure of the code collapses the origin search, and the decoder now searches only the four board orientations a camera can physically observe rather than all eight dihedral relabellings — a mirrored view of an opaque printed board is not reachable through a lens. What remains of this stage is mostly edge-dot sampling, which those changes do not touch, so the grid build is now the largest owned cost.

end_to_end.desc: Full detector (corner detection + grid build + decode) per public frame, p50.

comparison.desc: calib-targets vs OpenCV on recall and runtime, on the public report images. Runtime is each detector's native p50: OpenCV from cv2, ours from the Rust full_stage_timing measurement (corner detection + grid build + decode) — timing our detector through the Python binding would add marshalling overhead unrelated to detection.
comparison.caveat: OpenCV chessboard detection is all-or-nothing and needs exact board dimensions (the success column shows it returned the full board). small.png is a partial ChArUco view with no independent ground truth, so its row is a detected-count comparison, not recall-vs-GT. Our detector is partial-tolerant and self-identifying.
